topics: intro, current stack, traffic and budget constraints, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, batching and kv/prefix caching, quantization and model selection, next steps and pilot plan
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-14 16:00 UTC, Duration ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Li (Harbor Quant CTO), Sara Novak (Head of ML), Ravi Singh (Infra), Alex Moro (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we have Maya, Diego and Priya from Redwood and Evan, Sara, Ravi and Alex from Harbor Quant. Quick agenda - understand your workload and goals, dig into cost/unit economics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private, and agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:18] Evan: Yeah looks good. We mostly want to understand where we get predictable costs. We're doing prod recommendation scoring and a chat assistant for traders - so latency matters but so does cost.
[00:30] Sara: Right, volume is spiky. During market open we get bursts up to ~600 qps, but average around 80 qps. Token distribution: short prompts, like 50-150 tokens per request, responses 40-300 tokens depending on the task.
[00:45] Diego: Got it. A couple clarifying Qs - are you already running any LLMs in prod? Where are you hosting?
[00:55] Evan: We're partly on OpenAI hosted for prototyping, and self-hosting some smaller models on our k8s GPU fleet for cheaper batch jobs. We're trying to reduce per-inference cost and avoid vendor lock, but operational overhead is big.
[01:10] Priya: Makes sense. On Redwood Hosted, pricing is usage-based - per-token - and we also offer Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem). Typical hosted unit pricing (ballpark) for our curated open models is in the low single-digit cents per 1k prompt+completion tokens for higher-capacity models, but it varies by model and sequence length.
[01:35] Sara: Can you be more concrete? Our finance team wants $X/token numbers.
[01:40] Maya: Sure - just to get alignment, we often show 3 model tiers: small open models (cheap, quantized) ~ $0.0005 - $0.002 per 1k tokens; mid-size ~ $0.002 - $0.01 per 1k; large models or transformer + safety checks can push higher. For Dedicated, you amortize GPU cost - example: a reserved A100-equivalent pool for predictable throughput could bring effective per-1k-token costs down by 40-60% versus hosted for heavy sustained usage, depending on utilization and batching.
[02:12] Ravi: Those ranges are pretty wide. Our CFO asks about real examples for our traffic - how to estimate?
[02:20] Diego: We typically build a cost model: inputs are tokens per request, requests per second distribution, target latency SLO, model choice, and expected utilization. Batching and KV/prefix caching are the levers that change the effective tokens executed on GPU. For example, with a prefix cache for common prompt prefixes and 30% cache hit, your token generation work could drop proportionally.
[02:42] Alex: When you say batching, what's the latency tradeoff for our trader use case? We can't add big queueing delays.
[02:50] Priya: There's continuous batching in our runtime - it tries to batch only when it doesn't impact latency SLOs. For sub-100ms tail SLOs, batching windows are tiny; for 200-500ms you can get larger batches and better throughput. We can tune target latency and batch size policies per route. So for trading assistant, we would keep tight latency SLOs and rely more on caching/quantization; for backend scoring jobs you can use larger batches.
[03:17] Sara: We also need deterministic monthly costs for finance - open to commit to Dedicated but need to know break-even points.
[03:25] Diego: Break-even calc is straightforward: compare hosted per-token spend at your expected volume to monthly reserved cost of Dedicated. We'll run scenarios - e.g., if you have sustained 100 qps @ avg 150 tokens total per request, that's X tokens/day. We'll model both with and without 30-50% caching and different batching efficiencies.
[03:45] Evan: Is there an example benchmark you can share?
[03:48] Maya: We'll send a sample pricing spreadsheet with pre-filled scenario rows. Also, we can run a pilot on Hosted with your traffic to measure real cache-hit and batching gains and return estimated unit cost.
[04:00] Ravi: On Private - if we do VPC/private control plane, what's the delta on licensing? We might have regulatory/compliance reasons.
[04:07] Maya: Private has platform fee + support. There's an enterprise contract and then infra compute either runs in your cloud under our runtime or on-prem. The tradeoff: higher fixed cost but better control, and if you're already committing capital to GPUs, Private can be more economical when you account for data residency and audit requirements.
[04:25] Sara: KMS/HSM and audit logs are must-haves. We need SSO, RBAC, and per-token audit.
[04:30] Priya: We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and can push logs to your SIEM. KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options) are supported for Private and Dedicated - Hosted uses our multi-tenant KMS but we can discuss bring-your-own-key for Dedicated enterprise tiers.
[04:50] Alex: If we go Dedicated, how does autoscaling work? We have big spikes at market open.
[04:55] Diego: Dedicated pools have configurable autoscaling and reserved burst capacity. You can set policies to keep a baseline for latency-sensitive routes and allow elastic bursts for non-critical loads. For extreme bursts we can route to Hosted as overflow (fallback policy) to avoid cold-starts.
[05:12] Evan: Routing to Hosted as overflow - is that seamless and how about data egress?
[05:18] Priya: It's seamless at the API layer. Data residency concerns are real - we can configure routing by region, and for sensitive data we recommend Private or Dedicated where compute sits in your VPC. The overflow route can be to a sanitized model or to Hosted with stricter logging.
[05:35] Sara: We're trying to hit a target cost ceiling of $30k/month for inference at current expected growth - is that realistic?
[05:42] Diego: Depends on model and caching. Quick rough math: if you have 4M tokens/day, that's 120M tokens/month. At $0.002 per 1k tokens would be $240/month (wait, math check) - sorry, I need to confirm token counts.
[06:10] [laughter] Diego: Apologies, I messed the unit conversion. If it's 120M tokens, that's 120,000 * 1k tokens. At $0.002 per 1k that's $240. That sounds low - ok, we need to confirm token counts.
[06:22] Alex: I think we meant 40M tokens/day.
[06:26] Diego: OK 40M/day -> 1.2B/month -> 1,200,000 thousands * $0.002 = $2,400/month. Still below $30k. If you use very large models or have long completions, costs increase. Also add monitoring/throughput overhead. Dedicated fixed cost could be e.g., $30k-$60k/month depending on GPU fleet. So $30k could be either too high or tight depending on patterns.
[06:50] Evan: So it seems we need concrete pilot numbers.
[06:55] Maya: Agreed - we'll instrument a pilot and run your traffic for a week. We'll measure cache hit, batching gains, and tail latencies and give a line-item cost.
[07:05] Sara: One more technical Q - quantization/accuracy tradeoffs. Our models can't drift in quality much.
[07:12] Priya: We recommend trying 8-bit or 4-bit quant for certain models, run eval suites we can help with. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles by workload. We also provide regression alerting tied to a prompt/eval set. For QA-critical scoring, you may prefer higher-precision or keep model in hosted Private Dedicated where you can pin model versions.
[07:35] Ravi: For the pilot, what data do you need from us?
[07:38] Diego: A week of representative requests (synthetic or redacted), token distribution, endpoint definitions, and latency SLOs. We'll run the pilot on Hosted initially to avoid infra setup.
[07:48] Evan: Security gating: can we get SOC2 and network diagrams before we start?
[07:52] Maya: Yes, we'll attach SOC2, ISO, and a network diagram. We'll also include recommended redaction/PII patterns for the pilot.
[07:59] Alex: Great. Anything else?
[08:02] Maya: Recap of next steps: send pricing spreadsheet + cost model template, schedule pilot kickoff (propose Tue 2026-04-20), send SOC2/ISO + network docs, and technical deep dive for VPC/KMS.
[08:15] Evan: Sounds good.
[08:18] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional misnames (Ethan vs Evan) and some numeric noise when Diego did quick math. Real follow-ups: Redwood to run pilot and provide concrete per-token cost scenarios including caching and batching sensitivity.

References shared during call: "pricing_spreadsheet_v1.xlsx" (link), "pilot_playbook.md" (link), SOC2 + compliance packet (link).
